# The sources

## Insee

Here are the two links for the datasets that come from Insee :

- <https://www.insee.fr/fr/information/7672015> ;
- <https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/8736938>.

## Observatoire des Territoires

In reality, these datas come from different institutions but they are all accessible from the website of the "Observatoire des Territoires".

Here is the link : <https://www.observatoire-des-territoires.gouv.fr/outils/cartographie-interactive/#view=map80&c=indicator>

Sadly, the benefit of this website can also be a drawback because to have the same datasets as me, you need to remake the whole selection of the observations and the datas. But, at the scale of the city (there is more than 30,000 in France), the you can only select a few variables at a time because if you try to load more than 15/20 variables at a time then the website reload and you have to do the whole process again (I talk from a ... traumatizing experience ...).

## datagouv

The link is the following : <https://www.data.gouv.fr/datasets/revenu-des-francais-a-la-commune/reuses_and_dataservices>

# Description of the sources

With the first link to the website of Insee, we have access, for each city in France, to the codename of their "EPCI" (Etablissement Public de Coopération Intercommunale). It allows us to go from the scale of the city to the scale of multiple-ones when it seems more convenient (or logical) like for example if we want to see if people in one city have access to a family physician : we know that people, at least in France, are able to go relatively far away to see a physician (which is totally legitimate). Insee also provided me with informations about the pourcentage of population covered by the C2S (the free one and the contributing one) in each city that has more than 10,000 inhabitants (and most of cities of more than 5,000 inhabitants).

For the website of the "Observatoire des Territoires", I had access to informations about all French cities and EPCI on the following topics :

- demography (density, oldness, gender, etc) ;
- family matters (size of families, only one parent families, etc) ;
- work (legal statues, precarity, unemployement rate, etc) ;
- wages and wealth (poverty rate, median income, etc) ;
- education ;
- housing (housing prices, housing precarity, etc) ;
- healthcare providers ;
- general public services access ;
- social matters (RSA, APL, etc).

Lastly, le datas from datagouv give us the wages and wealthness of people in each city (Iris) in France.

# Loading the datas

## The libraries come first

```{r}
#| message: false
library(here)
library(vroom)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

## Then I begin with the Insee and datagouv datas (the easiest ones)

```{r}
#| message: false
table_communes <- read_xlsx(here("datasets", "table-appartenance-geo-communes-2023.xlsx"), skip = 5)
```

I needed to skip the 5 firsts rows of the dataset because they were empty.

```{r}
#| message: false
taux_c2s <- vroom(here("datasets", "beneficiaires_CNAM_01-01-2023_Iris_csv", "data_CNAM2023_COM.csv"))
```

This dataset is good, I don't need to do modifications at this moment.

```{r}
#| message: false
revenus_communes <- vroom(here("datasets", "revenu-des-francais-a-la-commune-1765372688826.csv"))
```

This dataset is good, I don't need to do modifications at this moment.

## Now, I import the fragmented datas

```{r}
#| message: false
data_1 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-1.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_2 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-2.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_3 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-3.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_4 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-4.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_5 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-5.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_6 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-6.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_7 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-7.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_8 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-8.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_9 <- vroom(here("datasets", "data-9.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
data_EPCI <- vroom(here("datasets", "data_EPCI.csv"), skip = 2, na = c("N/A - division par 0", "N/A - résultat non disponible"))
```

I will need to merge datasets from `data_1` to `data_9` but first, I need to address the problem of importation : the first (and sometimes, the second) line of the datasets is wrong. The second problem was the fact that the variables where recognized as characters and not doubles.

**DISCLAIMER : to resolve the problem of the the recognition of variables, I used AI Gemini --\> I asked it why my variables were not recognized as numbers and it said to me that it was because of the "N/A - division par 0" and the "N/A - résultat non disponible". It said it made R thinks that the variables are character and that I need to make clear that these observations are missing values.**

## Merging of `data_1` to `data_9`

```{r}
data_COM <- data_1 |> 
  inner_join(data_2, by = join_by(Code, Libellé)) |> 
  inner_join(data_3, by = join_by(Code, Libellé)) |> 
  inner_join(data_4, by = join_by(Code, Libellé)) |> 
  inner_join(data_5, by = join_by(Code, Libellé)) |> 
  inner_join(data_6, by = join_by(Code, Libellé)) |> 
  inner_join(data_7, by = join_by(Code, Libellé)) |> 
  inner_join(data_8, by = join_by(Code, Libellé)) |> 
  inner_join(data_9, by = join_by(Code, Libellé))
```

We have successfully merged `data_1` to `data_9` in a new dataset called `data_COM`.

# Description of the datas

| Dataset          | Number of rows               | Number of columns            |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| data_COM         | `{r} nrow(data_COM)`         | `{r} ncol(data_COM)`         |
| data_EPCI        | `{r} nrow(data_EPCI)`        | `{r} ncol(data_EPCI)`        |
| revenus_communes | `{r} nrow(revenus_communes)` | `{r} ncol(revenus_communes)` |
| table_communes   | `{r} nrow(table_communes)`   | `{r} ncol(table_communes)`   |
| taux_c2s         | `{r} nrow(taux_c2s)`         | `{r} ncol(taux_c2s)`         |


At this point, I think the more important variables are (for each Iris city) the number of people covered by the free C2S (`C_C2SNP` in `taux_c2s`) and the participative one (`C_C2SP` in `taux_c2s`). Since we have the total population of these cities, we can calculate the rate of C2S take-up. 

I also think that, for the first part of the project (calculation of the non take-up rate), variables such as the median of the income, the poverty rate and the D1 will be very useful. 

# My project

I want to make for the 1928 cities that we have in `taux_c2` an approximation of the non take-up rate for C2S. When it is done, I would like to find out what are the socials, demographics and economics reasons why there is non take-up. 
We know from the Drees (French Ministery of Health) that at the national scale, there is roughly 44% of non take-up (31% for free C2S and 66% for the contributive one). But the Drees only make assumptions of the reasons why there could be such a phenomena. 
So, I would like to do an econometrical study with cross-sectional datas to try to have a better understanding of this very high non take-up rate.
